issues.description: The template's PersonService declares a constructor that accepts a PersonRepository (constructor injection), while the solution's PersonService has a no-argument constructor that sets the personRepository field to null. This is a structural contradiction about how the repository dependency is provided. Students expect constructor injection (as present in the template) and will be guided to implement methods using an injected repository; the solution's no-arg constructor with a null final field is inconsistent and confusing with respect to dependency injection and bean wiring.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the dependency-injection approach consistent. Restore constructor injection in the solution by providing a constructor PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) that assigns the final field (matching the template), or alternatively change the template to use field/setter injection consistently and document it. Do not leave the final repository field initialized to null in the solution; ensure Spring can inject the repository (prefer constructor injection) so students are not confused about how to obtain the repository instance.
